work.title: Symphony No. 3 in C minor, Op. 78 “Organ”

version.value: First half of the symphony’s two large movements, as divided on the transferred 78 rpm set
version.note: The transferor describes the contents of sides 1–4. The labels do not give the tempo changes within each part.

value.name: Walter Hendl
value.role: piano, four hands (listed in James North’s discography; uncredited on the labels)

performers.note: The transferor says Nies-Berger is credited on all labels but plays only on sides 3, 4, 7 and 8, and that the piano players are uncredited; MusicWeb’s review of the Pristine reissue names Walter Hendl and Arthur Schuller as pianists.

date.note: Recorded on Monday 10 November 1947 per the transferor’s description; MusicWeb gives only “November 1947”.

label.note: Issued in the United States in June 1948; also issued in France, Italy, the Netherlands and Britain.

catalogue.note: Catalogue numbers as given by the transferor; no label has been inspected.

matrixTakeSides.note: The transferor prints the last matrix as XCO 38326, evidently a typing slip. Takes are not identified.

credits.note: The Internet Archive item was uploaded on 31 March 2022 by a private collector; no transfer engineer is named.

date.note: The Archive’s upload date is not a transfer date.

processing.note: The Archive supplies FLAC and a VBR MP3 derivative; equalisation and speed correction are not described.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of a 78 rpm transfer; the four sides of this half are joined in one file

composition.value: Public domain: Saint-Saëns died on 16 December 1921
composition.note: More than seventy years after the composer’s death.

recording.value: Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1948, before 1963
recording.note: The programme’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applies: the transferor documents the June 1948 issue as Columbia MM-747, Pristine and MusicWeb confirm the November 1947 session as Munch’s first American recording, and Columbia’s printed record catalog for 1949 lists the eight-side set MM-747 (Munch, Nies-Berger). The 1948 catalog does not list it, which fits a mid-1948 issue. This is not US or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

rights.creditLine: Camille Saint-Saëns, Symphony No. 3, Op. 78, Part I; Philharmonic-Symphony Orchestra of New York, Charles Munch, Édouard Nies-Berger (organ). Columbia Masterworks MM-747 (1948), Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only.

sources.title: Internet Archive — Saint-Saens Symphony No. 3 (Munch, 1947), Columbia MM-747
sources.locator: Description: session date and place, issue in June 1948, set and matrix numbers, side contents, anchors at 8:47 and 6:55, organ on sides 3, 4, 7, 8, first American recording; file inventory.

sources.title: Pristine Classical — Munch: The Complete New York Philharmonic Recordings (PASC448)
sources.locator: Munch’s first American recording; first recording of the work since Coppola’s 1930 set.

sources.title: MusicWeb International — review of Pristine PASC448
sources.locator: Session, November 1947, Carnegie Hall; organist Édouard Nies-Berger; pianists Walter Hendl and Arthur Schuller.

sources.title: Columbia Records Inc. — Columbia Record Catalog (1949)
sources.locator: Entry: Symphony No. 3 in C minor, Op. 78, Charles Muench conducting the Philharmonic-Symphony Orchestra of New York, E. Nies-Berger (organ), 8 sides, set MM-747. The Columbia Record Catalog (1948) at https://archive.org/details/columbiarecordca00unse has no such entry.
